items.title: Trust GitHub Actions to publish @gatetest/mcp-server on npm
items.unblocks: `git tag v1.61.1` → CLI 1.61.1 (bare npx fix, lib/site-url), MCP 1.2.0 (proxy crash fix), Docker image on ghcr, WordPress zip on the release. publish.yml fails at the MCP step until this exists.
items.step: npmjs.com → sign in → package @gatetest/mcp-server → Settings → Publishing access / Trusted Publisher → add GitHub Actions: organization or user `crclabs-hq`, repository `GateTest`, workflow filename `publish.yml`, environment blank → Save.

items.title: Tag and push v1.61.1
items.unblocks: publish.yml: CLI 1.61.1 on npm, MCP 1.2.0, Docker image on ghcr.io, WordPress zip attached to the GitHub release. Everything downstream of a release (wordpress-org-submit) waits on this.
items.step: On a clean main: `git checkout main && git pull && git tag v1.61.1 && git push origin v1.61.1`. Do it AFTER npm-trusted-publisher-mcp or the MCP publish step fails and the tag is burned.
items.where: Local clone of crclabs-hq/GateTest, on main

items.title: Create the GateTestHQ namespace on Open VSX and store OVSX_PAT
items.unblocks: Cursor / Windsurf / VSCodium installs of the extension — the Open VSX leg of publish-vscode.yml.
items.step: open-vsx.org → sign in with GitHub → accept the Publisher Agreement once → Namespaces → create `GateTestHQ` → Access Tokens → Generate New Token → GitHub: crclabs-hq/GateTest → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret `OVSX_PAT` = the token.

items.title: Store the VS Code Marketplace PAT as repo secret VSCE_PAT
items.unblocks: publish-vscode.yml publishes to the VS Code Marketplace without a manual .vsix upload.
items.step: dev.azure.com → User settings → Personal access tokens → New Token: Organization = All accessible organizations, Scopes = Marketplace → Manage → Create → GitHub: crclabs-hq/GateTest → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret `VSCE_PAT` = the token.

items.title: Set the missing production secrets on box 161 and restart gatetest-web
items.unblocks: Readiness Probe green (readiness-probe.yml); the homepage badge stops returning 503; Tallrig dispatch, recipe store and Gluecron bridge come alive.
items.step: ssh to box 161 → append to /opt/gatetest/website/.env.local: GATETEST_INTERNAL_TOKEN (also set the SAME value as the repo secret GATETEST_INTERNAL_TOKEN — the homepage badge 503s without it), GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, TALLRIG_API_TOKEN (mint a platform API key in the Tallrig dashboard), TALLRIG_DISPATCH_SECRET (shared HMAC — also set it in Tallrig's project store), GATETEST_RECIPE_STORE_TOKEN, GLUECRON_BASE_URL, GLUECRON_API_TOKEN → `sudo systemctl restart gatetest-web` → `curl https://gatetest.io/api/status` shows nothing missing.
items.where: box 161 over SSH: /opt/gatetest/website/.env.local; Tallrig dashboard for the API key; GitHub repo secrets for GATETEST_INTERNAL_TOKEN

items.title: Rotate CRON_SECRET everywhere, then copy it into the repo secret
items.unblocks: Cron Ticks workflow (cron-ticks.yml) stops failing 401, and the tick bearer stops being a value that also lives on the compromised box 158.
items.step: Tallrig (read-only, 2026-09-16) found Tallrig Cron already calls /api/scan/worker/tick and /api/watches/tick every 2 and 5 minutes with a bearer that matches box 161 — so the current CRON_SECRET is stored in cron-job headers on box 158, the compromised box: treat it as burned. After the 158 rebuild, over SSH, never in chat: generate a new value → /opt/gatetest/website/.env.local on 161 → restart gatetest-web.service → the two Tallrig cron jobs (ccj_gatetest_scan_worker, ccj_gatetest_watches) → GitHub repo secret CRON_SECRET. All in one sitting; the tick endpoints answer 401 to any caller still on the old value. Then decide which of the three callers to keep (Tallrig Cron is the one that should stay).

items.title: Rotate every production secret that also lived on box 158
items.unblocks: Closes the 2026-09-10 exposure: Stripe, GitHub App, OAuth, session and admin secrets stop being values an attacker may hold.
items.step: Tallrig verified (read-only, 2026-09-16) that the hosted preview project store on compromised box 158 has held these names since 2026-07-21, and its vault key left with the same bundle on 09-10 — treat every VALUE as exposed if it equals production on 161. Rotate at each issuer, then update /opt/gatetest/website/.env.local on 161 over SSH and restart gatetest-web.service; never paste a value in chat. Order: (1) STRIPE_SECRET_KEY + STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (dashboard.stripe.com → Developers → API keys: roll; Webhooks → endpoint → roll secret); (2) GitHub App gatetest-hq: GATETEST_PRIVATE_KEY (App settings → Private keys → generate new, delete old) and GATETEST_WEBHOOK_SECRET (App settings → Webhook secret); (3) GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET (OAuth app → generate new client secret) and GITHUB_TOKEN (revoke the PAT, mint a fine-grained one); (4) GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET (Cloud console → Credentials → reset); (5) SESSION_SECRET + JWT_SECRET_KEY (new random 32+ bytes; signs everyone out once) and GATETEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD; (6) ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (console → API keys → create, delete old; also the repo secret); (7) DATABASE_URL password (provider → reset role password). CRON_SECRET has its own item. Publishable Stripe key, client IDs, App ID, NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL are not secrets. (8) RESEND: 17 Sep — Resend paused the team after abusive mail as noreply@gatetest.io. GateTest's own key was not on 158, but gatetest.io is a verified domain on the same Resend team as the exposed Vapron and AlecRae keys, so any team key could send as us. Delete every key on the team, reset password, enable 2FA, audit members; then create ONE new key per product, sending-only and restricted to its own domain (Resend supports both), GateTest's into /opt/gatetest/website/.env.local on 161 → restart gatetest-web. Never a key on 158.
items.where: AI vendor console (API keys), https://github.com/crclabs-hq/GateTest/settings/secrets/actions, box 161 over SSH

items.title: Commit or discard the uncommitted changes in /opt/gatetest on box 161
items.unblocks: Deploy to production box (deploy-box.yml → deploy-on-box.sh) stops refusing to pull over a dirty tree.
items.step: ssh to box 161 → `cd /opt/gatetest && git status` → if the changes matter, commit them on a branch and push it; if not, `git checkout -- . && git clean -fd` (review the list first — .env.local is untracked and must stay) → re-run deploy-box.yml.

items.title: Fix App 3766251's permissions and events, make it public, list it in the Marketplace
items.unblocks: GitHub Marketplace App page — the install path the listing, the install page and marketplace-sync.test.js all describe. Rejected once on 2026-05-14; scripts/marketplace-preflight.js exists so the second submission is not.
items.step: Run `node scripts/marketplace-preflight.js` → App settings (App 3766251) → Permissions: contents write, statuses write, drop checks write → Subscribe to events: workflow_run + issue_comment → description from integrations/marketplace/listing.md → Save → Advanced → Make public → Marketplace → List in Marketplace → submit for review.

items.title: Re-publish the MCP registry entry under io.gatetest/gatetest
items.unblocks: An official MCP registry entry that matches the shipped server and the .io domain. The current `ai.gatetest.www/gatetest` entry is stale: 111 modules, names an AI vendor, lives on the dead .ai namespace.
items.step: `mcp-publisher login dns --domain gatetest.io` prints a TXT record → add it at the gatetest.io apex in Cloudflare DNS (Boss Rule #4) → finish the login → `mcp-publisher publish` with server.json named `io.gatetest/gatetest` → deprecate `ai.gatetest.www/gatetest`.
items.where: Cloudflare DNS for gatetest.io and the `mcp-publisher` CLI on a machine with the repo checked out

items.title: Submit the WordPress plugin to wordpress.org
items.unblocks: GateTest in the wordpress.org plugin directory — installs from the WP admin instead of a zip download.
items.step: After the v1.61.1 release exists: download the WordPress zip from the GitHub release → wordpress.org/plugins/developers/add → upload the zip → submit for review.

items.title: Remove the stale Resend DKIM record and add DMARC p=reject on gatetest.io
items.unblocks: Mail from gatetest.io cannot be spoofed with the leaked-key signature after the 2026-09-15 Resend abuse incident; receivers reject anything not signed by the re-keyed domain.
items.step: After the Resend key rotation: Cloudflare DNS → delete the stale `resend._domainkey` DKIM record until the domain is re-keyed in Resend → add TXT `_dmarc.gatetest.io` = `v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:<a monitored mailbox>` → verify with `dig TXT _dmarc.gatetest.io`. DNS is Boss Rule #4.

items.title: Require every status check on main so a red PR cannot merge
items.unblocks: No red merge can land on main; the GateTest Full Scan becomes a required check; PRs touching the same files stop auto-merging past each other.
items.step: Settings → Branches → main protection rule → Require status checks to pass before merging: tick every check that runs on PRs, and add 'GateTest Full Scan' once it runs on PRs → Require branches to be up to date before merging: on → disable 'Update branch' auto-merge for PRs touching the same files → Save.

items.title: Make the ghcr.io/crclabs-hq/gatetest container package public
items.unblocks: docker pull ghcr.io/crclabs-hq/gatetest works anonymously; the post-publish smoke stops reporting the image as missing; the Docker channel can go on the homepage
items.step: github.com/orgs/crclabs-hq/packages → gatetest (container) → Package settings → Danger Zone → Change visibility → Public. The image itself was pushed by docker-publish.yml on the v1.61.1 tag (registry answers 403 = exists but private).
